title: Teddy Bears Exist Because of a 1902 Bear Hunt 🧸
description:
How did the teddy bear get its name? In 1902 President Theodore Roosevelt refused to shoot a tied-up bear, a cartoon made the moment famous, and two toy makers in Brooklyn and Germany invented the teddy bear at almost the same time.

topic: The Story of the Teddy Bear: How It All Started
script: In nineteen-oh-two, a president refused to shoot one bear, and that's why your teddy bear exists. Here's how it all started, on a muddy hunting trip in Mississippi. It's November. President Theodore Roosevelt is out in the swamps, on a bear hunt with the state's governor. After days of searching, Roosevelt hasn't seen a single bear. So his guide, Holt Collier, tracks one down with the hunting dogs, and ties it to a tree. Everyone waits for the president to shoot. But Roosevelt says no. Shooting a tied-up bear isn't fair, so he refuses. A few days later, a cartoonist named Clifford Berryman draws the moment for the Washington Post. In his cartoon, the bear is small and scared, with big round eyes. Readers love it. Berryman keeps drawing that little bear for years, like Roosevelt's furry sidekick. Now jump to Brooklyn, New York. Morris and Rose Michtom run a small shop, selling candy and toys. They see the cartoon, and Rose sews a soft, stuffed bear. They put it in the window, with a sign that says, Teddy's bear. The story goes, they even wrote to Roosevelt to ask if they could use his name. The bears sell out fast. So many people want one, the Michtoms start a whole toy company, called Ideal. But here's the twist. At almost the same time, in Germany, a toy maker called Steiff was making bears too. Margarete Steiff started the company by sewing felt elephants. Her nephew Richard loved sketching bears, and he designed one with arms and legs that move. In nineteen-oh-three, he took it to a big toy fair in Leipzig. At first, almost nobody cared. Then an American buyer ordered three thousand. By nineteen-oh-seven, Steiff was making nine hundred seventy-four thousand bears. So the teddy bear was born twice, on two continents, at almost the same moment. Now look closely at a teddy from back then. Long snout, low forehead, skinny arms. It looks like a real bear. But scientists who measured old teddies found they slowly changed over the years. The snouts got shorter. The foreheads got bigger. The eyes got rounder. Teddy bears started to look like babies. Why? Because people pick the cutest one. Our brains are wired to love baby-like faces, so the cutest bears sold best, year after year. It's evolution, but in a toy shop. Today, teddy bears are everywhere. In two thousand, one Steiff bear, with sapphire and diamond eyes, sold at an auction in Monaco for two point one million dollars. And it's not just kids who love them. In one British survey, about a third of adults said they still sleep with a teddy. All because, more than a hundred twenty years ago, one president wouldn't shoot one bear. Next time: how some animals freeze solid, and wake up again.
key_facts: November 1902: on a hunt in Mississippi, guide Holt Collier tied a black bear to a tree and Roosevelt refused to shoot it as unsportsmanlike (NPS)
Clifford Berryman drew the scene for the Washington Post (NPS)
Morris and Rose Michtom of Brooklyn made a stuffed 'Teddy's bear'; the family said Roosevelt gave permission; they founded the Ideal Novelty and Toy Company
Richard Steiff designed a jointed bear (55 PB, 1902); at the 1903 Leipzig toy fair an American buyer ordered 3,000; by 1907 Steiff made 974,000 bears (Wikipedia)
Teddy bears' snouts shortened and foreheads grew over the decades (baby schema; Hinde & Barden 1985 and later studies)
2000: a Steiff Louis Vuitton bear with sapphire and diamond eyes sold for $2.1 million in Monaco
2012 Travelodge survey: 35% of British adults sleep with a teddy bear
